name: nlp_hf_classification
title: HuggingFace Trainer intent classifier with a datasets pipeline, a custom compute_metrics and a hand-rolled holdout pass
origin: hardening round 1, domain-nlp, 2026-09-13 - the commonest NLP fine-tune shape there is
note: `unsupported` rows are planted defects no rule's documented detection covers today. MLV101 at data.py:44 fires only under --dataflow ip, where the subscript projection carries the frame tag and pays one hop; the default local mode is silent and says so with an untagged_dataflow diagnostic (finding NLP-02).

expected.defect: the TF-IDF vocabulary and idf weights are fitted on every ticket, two lines before the split
expected.why: the held-out tickets shape the vocabulary and the document frequencies, so the reported holdout score is optimistic

expected.defect: the datasets holdout is cut with no seed=
expected.why: datasets.Dataset.train_test_split shuffles by default, so every run fine-tunes on a different four fifths and scores on a different fifth
the baseline is scored on a different fifth of the corpus on every run

expected.defect: compute_metrics hands the raw logits to accuracy_score instead of logits.argmax(-1)
expected.why: accuracy_score compares float logits with integer class ids, so the accuracy the Trainer logs every epoch is the chance rate and nobody notices, because it is a number rather than an error

expected.defect: the same logits are handed to f1_score
expected.why: the macro F1 reported for model selection is computed over continuous scores, not over predicted classes
predictions come back in a different order every run, so per-sample comparison and a reproducible confusion matrix are both impossible

expected.defect: the Trainer is given no eval_dataset and the TrainingArguments set no evaluation strategy
expected.why: four epochs run with nothing scored on held-out data, so there is no signal for early stopping or for picking a checkpoint

expected.defect: the hand-rolled holdout pass never calls model.eval()
expected.why: RoBERTa keeps its dropout active and its layer norms in training mode, so the accuracy printed is not the model's

expected.defect: the holdout pass is not wrapped in torch.no_grad()
expected.why: an autograd graph is built and thrown away for every batch of the test set

expected.defect: the model is moved to cuda but the batch never is
expected.why: a CPU tensor fed to a CUDA module raises at run time

expected.defect: the whole module is pickled rather than model.state_dict()
expected.why: the checkpoint carries the class path and stops loading the moment the code moves

expected.defect: nothing seeds transformers, torch or numpy
expected.why: neither the datasets split nor the fine-tune can be repeated

forbidden.why: the HuggingFace Trainer owns the optimisation loop; there is no hand-written update whose gradients could go unzeroed
backward() and step() live inside Trainer.train(), not in this file
there is no hand-written backward/step pair here whose order could be wrong
no backward() call appears anywhere in this project, let alone inside no_grad()
the only DataLoader in this file is the holdout loader; the training batches are built by the Trainer, which shuffles by default
roc_auc_score is given np.asarray(logits), a continuous score - wrong for multi_class='ovr', which wants probabilities, but not the hard-label mistake MLV306 describes
no nn.Module subclass is defined in this project - the model comes from from_pretrained
no submodule container is built here at all
encoded.train_test_split() is the split itself, not a transform fitted before one; the tokenizer map above it is stateless with respect to the labels

unsupported.defect: multi_class='ovr' requires probabilities that sum to one across the class axis; raw logits do not, so the AUC is computed over an un-normalised score matrix
unsupported.why: MLV306 models the opposite mistake - hard labels where scores belong - and no rule models 'scores that are not the normalised probabilities this metric documents'

unsupported.defect: the split is not stratified, so a four-class intent corpus with a long tail can lose a whole class from the holdout
unsupported.why: MLV117 (no stratify on a classification target) is a later-tier rule and is not built
